papers.title: Large Organismic Model: A Developmental Architecture for Embodied, Affective, and Self-Directed Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: We propose the Large Organismic Model (LOM), a developmental architecture for artificial intelligence. Rather than reporting the performance of an implemented system, this position paper formulates a testable computational hypothesis that integrates ideas from biology, developmental neuroscience, reinforcement learning, world models, developmental robotics, intrinsic motivation, and episodic memory. papers.title: The GEM BizLab as a learning lab for technology and innovation management
papers.summary: Learning Labs are increasingly used to support experiential and innovation-oriented education, yet the mechanisms through which they generate learning remain poorly understood. This paper examines the GEM BizLab, a technology-enabled Learning Lab designed for technology and innovation management education. Drawing on Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), the study analyzes thirteen student projects involving emerging technologies such as AI, robotics, haptics, and smart retail systems. papers.title: Robotic automation of Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan based on active vision
papers.summary: Abstract The lifespan assay in Caenorhabditis elegans is a highly repetitive and labor-intensive procedure that can lead to counting errors and delays in obtaining results. Technicians and researchers should devote their time to more intellectually demanding tasks rather than simply observing the movement of nematodes. Full automation remains a major challenge across many fields, and it is particularly beneficial in preclinical research such as lifespan assays. papers.title: Jacques Lecoq’s Embodied and Ecological Actor Training
papers.summary: This chapter argues that Jacques Lecoq’s pedagogy, which nurtures creative expression through embodied identification with the more-than-human world and operates through non-hierarchical group creation, can be understood as a form of ecological enquiry, one that functions less as a fixed technique and more as an epistemology: a living methodology. Jacques Lecoq founded his school in Paris in 1956.
